doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Pay and financial struggle in Manhattan
summary: He made thirty-five dollars a night at Condon's and found it hard to afford Manhattan on jazz wages.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Can I ask you what you would make on a typical night place like that?

No that’s confidential. No I’m just kidding. No back then? I remember making thirty-five bucks a night at Condon’s. I don’t remember what we made at the other places, seriously. I probably forgot it for a good reason. It was probably very easy to forget, not being very significant in the first place. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-
Was it a struggle then financially to make it, to stay alive?

Oh, yeah. Sure. To be able to afford even a toilet of an apartment in Manhattan on jazz wages. These days a lot of guys get into doing a variety of things, playing electric, getting a symphony gig or a pops orchestra gig or anything like that. I never went that way, partly because I was ignorant that that kind of thing could be done. It just didn’t make sense to me. I just wouldn’t have fit in with that I guess. To me the way I look at it now, that’s not out of the question now, as teaching and pontificating like I’m doing now is not completely out of the question as much as it seemed to be back then. Now I’m just a player.
